content: I'll read the test image to analyze the plant disease symptoms.

**Visual Analysis:**

- **Affected plant part**: Tomato stem at a node junction
- **Key observations**:
  - A pronounced tan/bleached stem canker is centered at the node (where the lateral branch connects to the main stem)
  - The lesion shows a pale, somewhat whitish/cottony appearance — suggestive of mycelial growth
  - The lateral branch to the right has completely collapsed, wilted, and dried up (brown, shriveled tissue)
  - The main stem above and surrounding foliage appears otherwise relatively healthy
  - The canker appears to be girdling the stem at the node, cutting off water/nutrient flow to the branch above

**Differential Reasoning:**

- **Sclerotinia Timber Rot** (Sclerotinia sclerotiorum): Causes bleached/tan stem cankers, often at nodes; white cottony mycelium is characteristic; leads to wilting/collapse of branches above the canker — matches well
- **Gray Mold** (Botrytis): Gray fluffy sporulation on soft rotted tissue — this lesion looks firmer and more bleached than typical Botrytis
- **Southern Blight**: Typically at soil level with very distinct white mycelial mats and mustard-seed sclerotia — lesion here is higher on the plant
- **Alternaria/Bacterial Canker**: Alternaria produces darker lesions; bacterial canker typically shows vascular browning with more systemic wilt

The bleached, dry canker at the node with white mycelial presence and localized branch wilt above the infection point is most consistent with **Sclerotinia Timber Rot**.
